findings.title: One Delivery, Divergent Reception
findings.claim: The same recited Qur'anic descent is healing and active mercy for receptive believers, while resistant reception turns that arrival into increasing loss.
findings.mechanism: At 17:82 the descent verb and Qur'an identify one medium; shifa and rahma name its benefit, increase/loss its contrary effect. Dawn recitation, truthful entry/exit, truth against falsehood, receiver response, mercy/favor, and demand for a controllable readable book make the contrast contextual rather than two messages.
findings.reader_payoff: The polarity is relational: one delivery has divergent effects with reception, not a uniform benefit or a second revelation.
findings.containment: The brink and commercial-loss claims are excluded for lack of independent triggers. Gradual delivery is only a qualified contrast with the on-demand book; no full revelation chronology or universal medical cure is asserted.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence and exact occurrences support the bounded relation, but its synthesis is multi-step and edge/commercial subclaims are unsupported.
